coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay South Block 9A
record.summary: 400 China Basin is a 148-unit, 100% affordable homeownership condominium development (8 stories, roughly 180,000 sq ft) in Mission Bay South, developed by China Basin Partners LLC (Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers), designed by Mithun with associate architect YA Studio, and built by a Nibbi Construction/Baines Group joint venture; it held its grand opening around September 26-October 2, 2025.

facts.value: 400 China Basin St (Mission Bay South Block 9A)
China Basin Partners LLC (also '350 China Basin Partners, LLC' in some OCII filings), a joint venture of Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers
Mithun (architect of record), with associate architect YA Studio and landscape architect GLS
148 (100% of units are below-market-rate affordable homeownership)
Sale prices restricted to households earning 80-110% AMI, individual units priced at 75/85/95/105% of AMI; average affordability target about 90% AMI
180,063 total building area (129,712 residential) per OCII's 2021 filing; SF YIMBY's 2025 completion article cites approximately 200,000; the architect's own page cites 165,000 on a 0.69-acre site
~85 (zoning allowed up to 90 for the block)
100% affordable, permanently price-restricted homeownership condominiums (OCII Limited Equity Program)
State of California Infill Infrastructure Grant funding, OCII permanent/gap financing (forgivable loan), homebuyer sales proceeds, and a private construction loan from Goldman Sachs
Type I (concrete) construction, U-shaped 8-story building over a podium; foundation uses roughly 200-ft driven piles due to Bay Mud fill conditions

Targeted GreenPoint Rating of 195 in 2021 planning (above the RFP's 125 minimum); reported as GreenPoint Platinum at completion, all-electric, with rooftop solar and a ground floor raised for sea-level-rise resilience
~34 spaces (0.23-0.25 cars/unit), unbundled from unit sales

costs.what: Total development cost, estimated at loan approval (TDC/unit $913,146)
Total OCII (public) investment/loan, after the Oct 2023 $8M increase
State of California Infill Infrastructure Grant (IIG)

open_questions: Exact ribbon-cutting date: the project's own press page cites Friday, September 26, 2025; SF YIMBY's Oct 2, 2025 article describes the ceremony as having happened 'last week' -- consistent but not independently confirmed against a third, non-developer source.

Square footage is inconsistent across sources: 180,063 sq ft (OCII 2021 filing) vs. ~200,000 sq ft (SF YIMBY 2025) vs. 165,000 sq ft (the architect's own page) -- possibly different measurement conventions, not resolved.
Final as-built total development cost was not located in a post-completion OCII/MOHCD document; the $135.1M figure is a pre-construction (Nov 2021) estimate.
OCII's Oct 2023 memo projected a temporary certificate of occupancy in August 2024, roughly 13 months before the Sept/Oct 2025 opening; no source explains the gap.
The general contractor's name appears variously as 'Nibbi Construction,' 'Nibbi Brothers' and 'Baines-Nibbi JV' across OCII documents -- treated as the same joint venture.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

record.notes: Mission Bay South Block 9A, 400 China Basin St -- 148 units of 100% affordable homeownership housing (8 stories, ~200,000 sq ft), developed by China Basin Partners LLC (Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers); architect Mithun. Construction began 2023 (OCII FY23-24 Annual Housing Production Report shows it 'nearly complete' that fiscal year); ribbon-cutting Oct 2, 2025 (sfyimby.com).
